title: A Waveform Window from a Debug Event Bus
description: Connect a subscriber to a debug event bus, prove that a dump started by a watchdog trigger misses the cause of a bus stall, and capture the cause with a two-run waveform window controlled from tb_top.

steps.title: Step 1: Run the starter and read the log
steps.instructions: Compile testbench.sv with tb_top as the top module and run it. The run ends with UVM_FATAL [WDG] at 5150 ns after the bus broadcasts WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT at 5100 ns ('no transfer for 2075 ns after 300 beats'). Work out when the last beat was accepted, and predict whether a dump started at the trigger would show why the beats stopped.

steps.title: Step 2: Add the subscriber and start a dump on the trigger
steps.instructions: In waveform_trigger_sub, get the global uvm_event 'dump_now' from uvm_event_pool in build_phase and trigger it from write() when the tag is WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT. Create trig_sub in dbg_env and connect bus.ap to trig_sub.analysis_export. Rerun and open after_trigger.vcd: it covers 5100 to 5150 ns only, with ready already 0. Explain why, using IEEE 1800-2023 §21.7.1.3.

steps.title: Step 3: Make the subscriber name the window
steps.instructions: In write(), compute start_ns = last_ok_ns - pre_ns (0 if negative) and print it with `uvm_info("WAVE_TRIG", ..., UVM_NONE). Rerun and confirm the log says 'Last transfer at 3025 ns: rerun with +DUMP_START=2825'.

steps.title: Step 4: Open the window in a rerun
steps.instructions: In tb_top's dump_ctl block, read +DUMP_START with $value$plusargs; if present, wait until that time and dump to window.vcd, otherwise keep the trigger behaviour. Rerun with the same seed and build plus +DUMP_START=2825. In window.vcd, find the rising edge at which tb_top.u_sink.ready falls and the value of accepted just after it.

steps.title: Step 5: Check your understanding
steps.instructions: Compare your files with solution.sv and answer the five questions in Step 5 of the README: single-pass capture, same seed and same build, why dump control lives in tb_top, what $dumplimit does, and how you would size the window for a 20-hour run.
